name: Outdoor On/Off Plug
description: A weather-resistant plug-in relay module for switching outdoor lights and appliances on and off remotely. It is rated NEMA 3R and works from -4 to 122 degrees Fahrenheit.

steps.text: Plug the appliance or device (the load) you want to control into the module's outlet, with the load's own switch in the on position.
Plug the module into an unswitched, weather-protected wall outlet with ground fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) protection.
steps.expect: Status LED turns solid green and the load turns on

steps.text: If the load does not turn on, tap the SET button.
Let the module hang down from the outlet.

notes: Use a 3-prong outlet with GFCI protection, or one protected by a GFCI device upstream; do not plug into a switched outlet, a filtered power strip or an AC line filter.
After installation the load's own switch no longer controls it unless load sensing is enabled.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps (3 seconds).

notes: As a controller: put the module in linking mode first, adjust the responder to the desired state, then press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps; the module's LED stops blinking.

As a responder: press and hold the controller's SET button until it beeps, use the module's SET button to set the load on or off, then press and hold the module's SET button until it double-beeps; the controller double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.
With the Hub, follow the app's instructions and, with the connected fixture on, press and hold the module's SET button when prompted.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps (3 seconds).
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder; the device makes no link back to the Hub.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.
Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps again.
steps.expect: LED blinks red; the module is in unlinking mode

notes: As a controller: then press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps; the module double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.
As a responder: put the controller in unlinking mode first, then press and hold the module's SET button until it double-beeps.

steps.text: Unlink the module from any controller that controls it.
Unplug the module.
While pressing and holding the SET button, plug the module back in; do not let go of the button.
steps.expect: Module emits a long beep and the Status LED turns green

steps.text: When the long beep stops, release the SET button.
steps.expect: Status LED flashes red and then turns green; after a few seconds the load turns on

steps.text: For each controller that controls the module, put the controller in unlinking mode.
Press and hold the module's SET button until it double-beeps.
For each responder the module controls, put the module in unlinking mode.
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps.

notes: The Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 Owner's Manual says to remove all of the module's responder links before uninstalling it, otherwise controllers keep retrying commands and create network delays, and to remove each responder link when removing the module from the network.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes give its identity as category 0x01 and subcategory 0x3A, which the catalog gives to the 2672.
Its owner's manual lists it as an Insteon controller; its Developer Notes list it as a responder only, as the catalog does.
sources: Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes
Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 Quick Start Guide
